structured_output.title: A base only matches at a path boundary: "/admin" no longer swallows "/admin-dashboard"
structured_output.premise: A Nuxt app served under baseURL "/admin/" has a page at "/admin-dashboard" (nuxt/nuxt#33924). ufo's withoutBase checked only that the input started with "/admin", so it cut those characters off and the router got "/-dashboard". withBase had the mirror bug: it treated "/admin-dashboard" as already carrying the base and returned it without adding "/admin/", so links pointed outside the app.
structured_output.verdict: Both functions now count the base as present only when the next character is "/", "?" or the end of the input. Four new tests that failed before now pass; every existing case is unchanged. Untested risk: a fragment right after the base ("/admin#top") no longer matches, so withoutBase leaves it alone and withBase adds the base again. Ask whether "#" should count as a boundary.

chapters.title: withoutBase stops cutting "/admin" out of "/admin-dashboard"
chapters.before: withoutBase("/admin-dashboard", "/admin/" or "/admin") sliced off "/admin" and returned "/-dashboard", so both tests failed.
chapters.after: The next character is "-", which is not a boundary, so it returns "/admin-dashboard" unchanged. "/admin/dashboard" still becomes "/dashboard".
facts: The new guard returns the input unchanged when nextChar is set and is not "/" or "?" (utils.ts:327-330).
Before the change, the only check was input.startsWith(_base), so any string prefix counted as a match.
Inputs with a real slash after the base, "/admin/admin-dashboard" and "/admin/dashboard", still become "/admin-dashboard" and "/dashboard" (trace 222-243).
The same fix applies whether or not the base has a trailing slash, because withoutTrailingSlash normalises both forms to "/admin".

open_questions.question: Does the stricter check still strip the base when a query or the end of the string follows it, as in "/api?test" or "/base"?

chapters.title: withBase now adds the base to "/admin-dashboard" instead of assuming it is already there
chapters.before: withBase("/admin-dashboard", "/admin/") saw startsWith("/admin") and returned "/admin-dashboard" unchanged, so both tests failed.
chapters.after: nextChar "-" fails the boundary check, so the input reaches joinURL("/admin", "/admin-dashboard") and comes back as "/admin/admin-dashboard".
facts: The early return now happens only when nextChar is missing, "/" or "?" (utils.ts:296-300). Any other input now reaches joinURL.
The joinURL path is new for these inputs (trace lines 77-82 and 99-104 marked +).
A caller that passed "/adminX" paths and relied on getting them back unchanged will now get "/admin/adminX".

open_questions.question: Do the older withBase cases (an empty base, a protocol URL, an input equal to the base) still behave the same?

chapters.title: withoutBase still strips the base when a slash, a query or the end of the string follows it
chapters.before: "/api?test" with base "/api" became "/?test", "/base" with "/base/" became "/", and "/base/a" became "/a".
chapters.after: Same results: nextChar is "?", missing, or "/", so the base is stripped as before. A "/" base or a protocol URL is still returned unchanged.
facts: "?" is explicitly allowed as a boundary, which keeps "/api?test" becoming "/?test" (trace 192-197).
When the input equals the base, nextChar is undefined and the base is still stripped ("/base/a" with base "/base/a/" becomes "/").
"#" is not in the allowed set. withoutBase("/admin#x", "/admin") used to return "/#x" and now returns the input unchanged. No test covers this; it is a reading of the code only.

answers.answer: Yes. "/api?test" still becomes "/?test", and an input equal to the base becomes "/", because "?" and a missing next character both count as boundaries.

chapters.title: withBase still leaves inputs that already carry the base, empty bases and absolute URLs alone
chapters.before: "/base" or "/base/a" with base "/base/" were returned unchanged, "/bar" became "/foo/bar", and "https://test.com" was returned untouched.
chapters.after: Identical results. The boundary check passes on end-of-string or "/", and the isEmptyURL and hasProtocol early returns run before the new code.
facts: A base of "/" or an input with a protocol returns before the new check (utils.ts:291-293).
Inputs that do not start with the base were already sent to joinURL, so they are unaffected.
Untested: withBase("/admin#x", "/admin") used to return the input unchanged and now goes through joinURL, producing "/admin/admin#x".

answers.answer: Yes. All ten original withBase cases return the same values, because the early returns run first and the boundary check passes on "/" or end-of-string.
